source_identity_policy: C-series IDs are critic-stage records for sources independently opened during this review. They do not reuse or silently rebind the investigator's S-series IDs. Exact per-page fetch timestamps are unavailable from the browser tool; accessed_utc records the nearest directly observed UTC clock capture.

records.title: Automerge Rust 0.12.0 Automerge API and author/actor behavior
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0; versioned docs.rs API page.
records.locator: Authors and Actors; with_author/set_author/get_author_for_actor; apply_changes; save; get_heads.
records.review_method: Opened the versioned API page; read the author/actor, apply_changes, save, and heads descriptions.
records.observed_operation: Changes can carry an Author ID; changes have no author when none is set. apply_changes ignores already-applied changes. save serializes the whole document; get_heads exposes the current change heads.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Author metadata is optional and is not authenticated crew identity by itself. Duplicate-change idempotence applies to identical document changes; it does not state that stateful sync messages can be replayed or regenerated safely.
records.applicability: Supports multi-value conflict presentation and point-in-time reads only if the application sets and maps trusted author IDs. Local durable storage and relay behavior remain app responsibilities.

records.title: Automerge Rust 0.12.0 ReadDoc source
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0; versioned source rendered by docs.rs.
records.locator: ReadDoc get_all/get_all_at and get_cursor/get_cursor_moving source documentation.
records.review_method: Opened the exact source link from the versioned ReadDoc API.
records.observed_operation: get_all returns conflicting values with the operation ID that created each value; *_at APIs read at supplied ChangeHash heads. Cursors address list/text sequence positions and define behavior when referenced items are removed.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Operation IDs are not displayed human names; an application must retrieve/map author information. A cursor is not a cue entity ID.
records.applicability: Supports candidate enumeration and publication reads at fixed heads; it does not supply the conflict UI or comment identity policy.

records.title: Automerge Rust 0.12.0 Transaction and Transactable API
records.released_version_or_commit: Rust crate automerge 0.12.0; versioned docs.rs API page.
records.locator: Transactable implementation method list: insert, delete, splice, splice_text; linked manual transaction source.
records.review_method: Opened the versioned Transaction API and its linked manual_transaction.rs source.
records.observed_operation: The inspected Rust transaction surface exposes list insertion, deletion, and splice operations. It does not document a high-level cue move operation in the inspected list API.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a library API observation, not proof that an app-level move-intent algorithm is impossible. List mutations still require a defined application-level semantic policy.
records.applicability: The proposed move-intent layer is necessary to give cue reorder human meaning; its conflict and materialization behavior needs specification and tests.

records.title: Automerge official list guide
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official Automerge documentation, accessed 2026-10-12; examples are JavaScript.
records.locator: Entity-map plus ID-list example and fine-grained-update guidance, around page lines 101–134.
records.review_method: Opened the official list guide and read the example and explanatory caveat.
records.observed_operation: Fine-grained edits to an entity map and ID list avoid replacing an entire nested document object and merge better under concurrent updates.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: JavaScript example and general modeling guidance; not a guarantee that an arbitrary cue order structure satisfies move semantics.
records.applicability: Supports separating stable cue records from order IDs while leaving the exact move policy to the application.

records.title: Automerge official merge rules
records.locator: Map merge rules and list merge rules, especially list element IDs, predecessor references, and reverse-insertion caveat.
records.review_method: Opened page directly and inspected the list merge rules.
records.observed_operation: List operations refer to element IDs; insertions refer to predecessor elements; concurrent insertions are deterministically ordered. The docs describe cases where insertion order is not preserved, especially reverse insertion.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The page describes low-level merge behavior and does not define an atomic user-intent move operation.
records.applicability: Supports caution against equating convergent list order with rehearsal crew intent.

records.title: Extending JSON CRDTs with Move Operations
records.released_version_or_commit: Da and Kleppmann, arXiv v2 revised 2024-03-19; PaPoC 2024 paper.
records.review_method: Opened the primary arXiv version record and abstract.
records.observed_operation: The paper identifies duplicates/cycles as possible in naïve concurrent move merges and says Automerge integration was planned.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Research result, not evidence that a released Automerge version exposes this move algorithm.
records.applicability: Supports treating the paper as motivation for explicit move conflict handling, not as a selected shipped feature.

records.title: Automerge official conflict guide
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official Automerge documentation, accessed 2026-10-12; JavaScript API example.
records.locator: Concurrent map assignments and conflict/getConflicts explanation, especially lines 109–112.
records.review_method: Opened the official conflict guide and read the concurrent assignment explanation.
records.observed_operation: Concurrent map writes retain multiple values while exposing a deterministic visible winner ordered by operation ID rather than wall clock; a later assignment can resolve the visible conflict set.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Guide uses JavaScript API names; the Rust-facing method is verified separately by C02. A deterministic winner is not a human decision.
records.applicability: Supports rejecting timestamp arbitration and using an explicit review UI.

records.title: Automerge Rust sync lost-message issue #1284
records.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2026-02-13; no target crate version named; maintainer response dated 2026-02-13.
records.locator: Reporter reproduction and maintainer response at issue lines 243–284; response says reliable in-order stream and reset state if a message may be dropped.
records.review_method: Opened the primary repository issue and inspected the report and maintainer response.
records.observed_operation: A generated but dropped message followed by offline edits can cause a nonterminating sync loop in the reproducer; preserving the exact unsent message avoids that reproduction. Maintainer says possible message loss requires resetting sync state.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: Open report, no target version named; not proof that all releases fail or that either relay-recovery proposal has been tested.
records.applicability: Directly relevant reconnect hazard; precise durable frame/state/ack behavior must be validated against the selected Rust version and adapter.

records.title: Automerge official collaborative text guide
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official Automerge documentation, accessed 2026-10-12; examples are JavaScript.
records.locator: updateText frequency guidance near the end of the page.
records.review_method: Opened the official text guide and inspected the updateText frequency caveat.
records.observed_operation: The JavaScript updateText helper produces worse merges when full-value diffs are infrequent; guidance is to update frequently, ideally per keystroke.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: JavaScript API guidance, not proof about the native Rust/Slint adapter or semantic overlap detection.
records.applicability: Supports requiring fine-grained Rust text operations and testing offline concurrent timing-note edits.

records.title: Yrs release history
records.released_version_or_commit: Release page showed v0.28.0 at commit 23b7f56, released 2026-09-17; v0.27.3 at ac476a4.
records.review_method: Opened the primary GitHub release list and inspected both release entries.
records.observed_operation: The release record confirms v0.28.0 and its commit; v0.27.3 lists fixes for insertion at index 0 and StickyIndex right association.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: A release record confirms release identity and stated change notes, not absence of unrelated bugs or behavior in every target workload.
records.applicability: Confirms the candidate version named in the investigator draft. I did not independently revalidate the investigator's Yrs 0.28.0 API claims in this review.

records.title: Automerge Repo storage/network documentation
records.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation, accessed 2026-10-12; examples use JavaScript @automerge/automerge-repo.
records.review_method: Opened the official repository documentation and read the introduction and adapter example.
records.observed_operation: The docs describe local storage adapters combined with zero or more network adapters and explicitly call this additional application plumbing.
records.governing_condition_default_exception: The documented Repo API is JavaScript; it is not an off-the-shelf Slint/Rust adapter or a production relay recommendation.
records.applicability: Supports the draft's statement that Rust persistence and relay glue remain application work.

review_limitations: Direct opens for the docs.rs Yrs 0.28.0 API pages returned an internal error. The reviewer relied only on the carried investigator source-map for those specific Yrs API statements and independently confirmed the release record.
The assignment's input map excludes the investigator's native Goal receipt and any direct execution logs; those process claims remain unverified in this critic review.
